claim.summary: For binary affine-product rows with independent factors per row, if every ordered graded colon through coefficient degree D-r_i equals the previous top ideal plus own linear factors, the Boolean static row filtration is strict through D and equals ordinary degree-D PC closure; its graded quotient is the top ideal quotient and it excludes one. At only coefficient degree D-r_i, top-step strictness and PC equality hold, with nonrefutability conditional on one absent at D-1. D>=max(2,r_i).
claim.assessment: Working binary specialization of Taylor syzygy lifting: ordered colons generate Koszul and own-factor syzygies, whose exact binary lifts prevent degree falls. No generic colon assertion or extension-field Boolean generalization.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Reusable conditional bridge from graded syzygies to ordinary PC; the lifting mechanism is already recorded, with binary factor idempotence supplying the new scoped application. No unrestricted source estimate.
significance.next_action: Seek actual source or unsatisfiable family satisfying the paid colon conditions; a top Hilbert series alone is insufficient.

claim.summary: For binary affine lifts of the source-owned one-dependency configuration n=2m-1, m>=2, first m-1 pair planes disjoint and last plane meeting their sum in a line with nonzero component on every pair, static row spans are strict and equal PC through m, with graded values given by ((1+2z)^m+z^(m+1))/(1+z). Every such affine system is satisfiable.
claim.assessment: Filtered application of the pinned Near-half graded proof; its series remains source-owned. The extra last-row colon homology first occurs in degree m-1. Satisfiability is proved by an affine-hyperplane factor-value argument.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Calibration of the binary lifting criterion, not an unsatisfiable near-half family or a new graded-series claim.
significance.next_action: Keep the satisfiability control when seeking higher-dependency or wider-row applications.

claim.summary: Taylor glue over a z-injective base: over F_3, let a base containing every x_i^2 - x_i have homogenization A = F[x,z]/J z-injective in degrees < D (equivalently V_s cap P_{<=s-1} = V_{s-1}), and add product constraints C = prod_j h_(C,j)(L_j) with factors L_j - a or chi_a(L_j) = 1-(L_j-a)^2 on affine F_3 forms; no generator or constraint a nonzero constant. If for every s <= D the signed top syzygies in G = A/zA are spanned by the Frobenius syzygies g l_j^(3-b_(C,j)) e_C and, for coherent pairs, g(c_C' l^(b-b_C) e_C - c_C l^(b-b_C') e_C') with b = max(b_C, b_C'), then every NS functional through k <= D extends through D, NS = PC through D, and there is no PC refutation of degree D. No robustness or member fall condition is used. With the closed base as base, this Taylor-generation condition replaces hypotheses (b) and (c) of relative gluing; for a single constraint it asks that the annihilator of its top be generated by the Frobenius powers up to pair syzygies, which freeness over F[l]/(l^3) implies but not conversely.
claim.assessment: Working proof after two fresh-context review passes; generalizes the Taylor glue theorem from the functional matching base and selectors to any z-injective base and coherent product constraints.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Gives relative gluing's conclusion over the closed base from (a) plus one Taylor-generation condition, so (b) and (c) become a single testable condition; does not remove the content of (c).

claim.summary: Single-degree Taylor lift: over F_3, in the setting of thm:based-taylor-glue (base with Booleanity generators, product constraints with factors L-a or chi_a(L)), fix one degree D; if the base is z-injective at D (V_D cap P_{<=D-1} = V_{D-1}) and the degree-D signed top syzygies are spanned by the Frobenius and coherent-pair syzygies, then V'_D cap P_{<=D-1} is contained in V'_{D-1} (no fall at level D), and if also 1 is not in V'_{D-1} the PC closure through D lies in V'_D and there is no PC refutation of degree D. So A3's Tor vanishing through 22k may be replaced by Taylor generation at any single degree D' >= 22k where the weak base is z-injective, plus a Nullstellensatz design at D'-1.
claim.assessment: Working proof after a fresh-context review; a refinement of thm:based-taylor-glue (one degree of Taylor generation and z-injectivity, with the design one degree lower assumed).

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: Splits A3 into a single-degree Tor condition at a freely chosen degree and a Nullstellensatz condition, which gives the dense core a degree to choose.
significance.next_action: Bound the single-degree Taylor defect for random dense tops with the class-survival machinery and identify the Nullstellensatz requirement at D'-1.
